title: Manage Kubernetes Clusters for GPU Infrastructure with NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA open-sourced (public preview, Apache 2.0) NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR) so AI factories and GPU clouds can run their own managed-Kubernetes service on bare-metal GPU infrastructure — NVKR builds version-pinned validated images, NVKE provisions tenant clusters via REST API using NICo. Firmus and SK Telecom are integrating it, alongside partners Mirantis, Rafay, Spectro Cloud, OpenNebula, vCluster and Netris; not yet production-ready.

insights.claim: NVIDIA released NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR) as open-source (Apache 2.0) public-preview projects that let AI factories run an EKS-style managed Kubernetes service on their own GPU infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is supplying neoclouds with the managed-Kubernetes layer hyperscalers built in-house, narrowing a key software gap between GPU clouds and AWS/Azure/GCP.
insights.locator: NVIDIA is announcing two open source projects

insights.claim: AI factory customers want to consume GPU capacity through familiar Kubernetes APIs with the factory operating the clusters, which requires API-driven provisioning, tenant isolation, upgrades, recovery and service commitments plus qualification across GPU generations and Kubernetes versions.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Operating managed K8s on GPUs is a costly capability barrier for smaller GPU clouds; an NVIDIA-provided stack lowers it.
insights.locator: AI Factory customers often want to consume

insights.claim: NVKE/NVKR leave AI factories in control of their software, operations, service and customer experience, and can be adopted together or independently — NVKE has no runtime dependency on NVKR and NVKR can build artifacts for other Kubernetes management systems.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Positions NVIDIA as enabler rather than competitor to GPU-cloud partners, easing adoption.
insights.locator: NVKE and NVKR divide this work

insights.claim: NVKE and NVKR are in public preview with APIs subject to change and are not yet recommended for production workloads.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Revenue/operational impact for partners is a 2027+ story; watch for GA.
insights.quote: NVKE and NVKR are not yet recommended for production workloads.
insights.locator: Both NVKE and NVKR are components

insights.claim: NVKE's management plane (REST API and controllers) runs on a management cluster bootstrapped by nvkectl via a temporary kind seed cluster, and creates per-customer workload clusters with their own control plane, etcd and node pools using bare-metal machines from NVIDIA Infra Controller (NICo) through the CAPNICo Cluster API provider.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: NVIDIA now owns the bare-metal lifecycle through tenant cluster layer for GPU clouds — deeper software lock-in into the DSX stack.
insights.locator: nvkectl starts a temporary seed cluster

insights.claim: NVKR builds node images, container images and Helm charts from version-pinned sources and records every build input, defining validated combinations of software versions and GPU generations so images are reproducible.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Reproducible validated recipes reduce qualification cost per GPU generation for operators.
insights.locator: NVKR defines the Kubernetes software configuration

insights.claim: AI factories publish release sets (machine image, cluster release, node pool release) so customers pick a validated Kubernetes version by name without handling OS images or cloud-init.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Productizes GPU-cloud K8s offerings in a hyperscaler-like UX.
insights.locator: Publish a release set that customers will run

insights.claim: NVKE requires nodes to present an attested SPIFFE identity before receiving join credentials, uses an OpenTelemetry-based telemetry pipeline, and is a Certified Kubernetes AI Platform and Certified Kubernetes Installer conformance tested on Kubernetes 1.36.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Conformance and security attestation are prerequisites for enterprise/sovereign tenants on GPU clouds.
insights.locator: NVKE is a Certified Kubernetes AI Platform

insights.claim: Inside workload clusters, NVIDIA's DSX stack adds AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) for GPU runtime, NodeWright for node packages and NVSentinel for break-fix automation.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Shows breadth of NVIDIA's AI-factory software portfolio layered on top of its hardware.

insights.claim: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Firmus and SK Telecom are integrating NVKE and NVKR into their AI factories to deploy Kubernetes clusters hosting AI workloads.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Early neocloud/telco adopters; signals NVIDIA's software reach into sovereign and regional AI clouds.
insights.locator: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Firmus and SK Telecom

insights.claim: Mirantis, Rafay, Spectro Cloud, OpenNebula Systems and vCluster are integrating NVKE/NVKR components into their managed Kubernetes offerings, and Netris is enabling NVKE for network automation.
insights.speaker: Nathan Taber
insights.so_what: Independent K8s-management vendors are aligning with NVIDIA's reference stack rather than competing — watch for differentiation erosion among them.
